name: Catalyst management (handling, regeneration, recycling)
principle: Catalyst is a consumable with a managed life: fresh catalyst is loaded under inert atmosphere with density and distribution control; activity declines through coking, poisoning and sintering and is watched via bed pressure drop and product quality; spent catalyst is unloaded (often under inert, sometimes offline via skimming), then either regenerated in-situ or sent to a specialist reclaimer that recovers metals and reconditions the carrier. Life-cycle contracts bundle supply, loading, surveillance and disposal so the refiner pays for active-days rather than tonnes.

process_steps.name: Fresh catalyst loaded with inert-atmosphere handling and loading-density control
Activity tracked through temperature profiles, pressure drop and product quality
Regenerated in-situ (controlled burn) or sent for ex-situ regeneration
Spent catalyst reclaimed: metals recovered, carrier reconditioned or disposed
